title: Fracture mode is a load-transfer property
caption: Eight parallel strips (armchair slit array) fail row by row and keep carrying 8 to 10 N/m to 25% strain; three wide rows with 15% width dispersion cascade in one avalanche at 14% strain. Many parallel paths of moderate dispersion share the released load; few wide paths cannot. Screened REBO2, athermal quasi-static uniaxial tension along x; colour: energy change per atom relative to the relaxed state (eV); red rings: atoms that have lost a bond; frames between stored quasi-static states are interpolated. All statements are model results.
slow_motion: 3x within ±0.0025 strain of first damage, peak load and major propagation
text_in_movie: chart axis labels and colour-bar numbers only
colour: energy change per atom relative to the relaxed state (eV), inferno colour map truncated at 0.9
chart: 2D stress (N/m) against engineering strain, one curve per panel in the panel's frame colour, moving marker at the current state
